KR1.heard: A.I. business operators shall submit the results of implementing the measures pursuant to each subparagraphs of paragraph, one to the Minister of Science and ICT.

KR2.heard: The Minister of Science and ICT may require that AI business operators submit relevant data or have public officials conduct necessary investigations in any of the following cases.

CA1.heard: Publish the modified Frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.

CA2.heard: Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report.

CA3.heard: Transmit to the Office of Emergency Services a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk, resulting from internal use of its frontier models every three months.

CA4.heard: Frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident, pertaining to one or more of its frontier models, to the Office of Emergency Services, within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident.

CA5.heard: Developers shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction.

CA6.heard: Establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident.

CA7.heard: Information to the Attorney General, a federal authority, a person with authority over the covered employee, or another covered employee who has authority to investigate, discover, or correct the reported issue.

CA8.heard: Provide a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose information to the large frontier developer.

CN2.heard: A mechanism for handling public complaints and reports on AI risks and hazards should be established.

CN3.heard: Developers creating products for commercial use should generate detailed test reports, analyze security issues and propose improvement plans.

G7-1.heard: facilitating third-party and user discovery and reporting of issues and vulnerabilities after deployment, such as through bounty systems, contests or prizes.

G7-2.heard: This should include publishing transparency reports containing meaningful information for all new significant releases of advanced AI systems.

PC1.heard: We agree to publish the non-sensitive findings of our evaluations in a standardized format to ensure comparability, while also creating a publicly accessible shared repository.

PC2.heard: Commit to disclose model capabilities, limitations and known risks.

PC3.heard: Share timely information on serious cyber and AI control incidents and other material precursor signals of serious harm, whether it's between companies and government, between governments or between AI companies.

PC4.heard: Policymakers commit to offer secure and confidential channels through which whistle-blowers, including employees and other relevant stakeholders, can raise concerns about systemic risks.

PC5.heard: Real-time monitoring of emergent capabilities, rigorous internal red teaming and transparent reporting lines that protect internal researchers.

NY1.heard: Publish the modified Frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.

NY2.heard: Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report.

NY3.heard: A large frontier developer shall transmit to the office a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk, resulting from internal use of its frontier models every three months.

NY4.heard: Report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the office within 72 hours from a determination that a critical safety incident has occurred.

NY5.heard: The frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction.

NY6.heard: The office shall establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident.

NY7.heard: No large frontier developer may develop, deploy or operate a frontier model in whole or in part a New York state without having a current disclosure statement filed with the office.

BIS1.heard: Reports regarding any export, re-export, or transfer in country. Subject to the provisions of this section are due no later than the first business day of the month following the transaction.

BIS2.heard: The exporter, re-exporter, or transferrer must inform the recipient that a BIS authorization is required if the item or items will be used at a data center to provide access to more than 12 million.

BIS3.heard: Reports are due by February 15 of each year, and must cover the period from January 1 through December 31 of the prior year.
